You can enchant an already-crafted item after the fact. Here's how it works:

Go to the **Artifact Foundry** — that's where enchanting happens. Each enchantment level adds 100 IP.

The materials work progressively: **Runes** enchant to .1, **Souls** to .2, and **Relics** to .3. You can only go one level at a time, so to reach .3 you'd enchant to .1 first, then .2, then .3.

The tier of the item determines which tier of runes/souls/relics you need — Tier X gear requires Tier X enchanting materials.

One caveat worth noting: this applies to already-crafted base items. You cannot change the enchantment level of a weapon that was crafted with enchanted materials baked in — that path is locked at craft time. But a plain unenchanted item? Totally upgradeable at the Artifact Foundry post-craft.

Resources are materials that are gathered from the environment or from skinning animals. Resources can be used to create Weapons, Armors, and Buildings in Albion Online. Resources that are gatherable from the open-world are: Fiber, Hide, Ore, Wood, and Stone. As with all other game elements, resources are divided into eight tiers. To gather any resource, the appropriate tool is required for each type of gathering. A tool can be used for harvesting any materials of its own tier and below; and the unenchanted version one tier higher. The tool does not need to be equipped; it must simply be in the player's inventory. Each resource must first be refined at their corresponding crafting building before it can be used in crafting. Tier 4 - 8 resources may be found in normal, uncommon, rare, exceptional or pristine enchantments. To harvest a enchanted resource, a tool of the same tier or higher as the resource must be used.

All resources can spawn enchanted. For fiber, hide, ore, and wood, weapons, and armor crafted with the enchanted refined resources will be stronger, their Item Power increasing by 100 per enchantment rarity. In contrast, the enchanted stone is treated as multiple unenchanted stones for refining purposes, as there are no enchanted refined blocks (uncommon stone is worth 2x regular stone, rare worth 4x regular, and exceptional worth 8x regular.) Enchanted resources spawn in four(4) varieties excluding unenchanted. They are uncommon, rare, exceptional, and pristine, by order of increasing rarity and power. Often, players will refer to unenchanted as "flat", uncommon as ".1", rare as ".2", exceptional as ".3" and pristine as ".4". Enchanted resources can only spawn from T4 and upwards. Gathering them will yield increased gathering fame. NOTE: pristine resources only spawn in the Outlands and will be indicated on the world map if you are close enough.

Albion Online Enchanting Explained.

Albion Online is a game that has enjoyed considerable popularity over the years. Players praise the huge world, enjoyable gameplay, and the fact that the game by Sandbox Interactive GmbH is available for free. In this MMORPG we have many opportunities to increase the power of our character and the equipment we have. In the following guide we will present the basics related to enchanting.

Enchanting in Albion Online

Enchanting a particular piece of equipment raises its stats, making our character more effective in battle. Upgrading equipment is possible with runes, souls and relics. Equipment can be upgraded three times using the aforementioned items.

  1. Enchanting from 0 to 1 - we use runes
  2. Enchanting from 1 to 2 - we use souls
  3. 

Enchanting from 2 to 3 - we use relics

We can strengthen the equipment ourselves, or buy already enchanted gear. In the case of low tier items it is worth doing it yourself, as you can save a lot of silver, a currency that is especially needed at the beginning of the game. When upgrading, it is worth paying attention to Item Power. The higher the value of this stat, the more potential the item has.

However, if we use high tier weapons, for example, tier VIII, the best choice would be to buy an already upgraded weapon. For example:

Tier VIII The Hand of Khor costs about 4.1 million silver. If we decide to enchant such z weapon ourselves, we will have to buy relics for a value of about 11 million silver. The costs are the same regardless of tier — T7 uses T7 runes/souls/relics, but the quantities are identical to any other tier. Here's the full breakdown for getting a flat T7 (Grandmaster's) item to .3 (three purple orbs):

**Step 2: .1 → .2** — T7 Souls
**Step 3: .2 → .3** — T7 Relics

| Item Type | Runes (→.1) | Souls (→.2) | Relics (→.3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Helmet, Boots, Cape, Off-hand | 96 | 96 | 96 |
| Chest armor, Bags | 192 | 192 | 192 |
| One-handed weapon | 288 | 288 | 288 |
| Two-handed weapon | 384 | 384 | 384 |

chat_messages.text:
The Tetragrammaton is יהוה — four Hebrew letters: Yod, He, Vav, He.

You're right that the letters carried sounds that don't map cleanly onto modern English pronunciation. Here's what each likely sounded like in ancient Hebrew:

- **י (Yod)** — a "Y" sound, like the start of "yes"
- **ה (He)** — a breathy "H" sound, aspirated, like a real exhale
- **ו (Vav)** — this is the contested one. In ancient Hebrew it was almost certainly a "W" sound, not the modern Israeli "V." Think of it like the English "W" in "water"
- **ה (He)** — same breathy H again, though at the end of a word in Hebrew it often goes nearly silent, just a breath

So the scholarly reconstruction most commonly used is **"Yahweh"** — said roughly: **"YAH-weh"**, two syllables, soft W, the ending breath barely voiced.

The older form **"Jehovah"** is considered a historical misreading — medieval scribes combined the consonants of YHWH with the vowel markings of *Adonai* (the substitution word) as a reminder not to pronounce it, and Christian readers took it literally.
